title: Measured recovery by ecosystem
subtitle: measured numbers, disrobe's own except where a row names another tool; sources cited per value in this file
note: Every value here is produced by a committed test gate or a local measurement harness. The source field cites the exact file:line that asserts or computes it. Numbers that could not be sourced from a gate are omitted by design.

verified_by.conditional: The published figure itself is gated unconditionally: the run asserts both corpora exist, then asserts proven-correct at or above this bar's own numerator regardless of environment. groups.heading: WebAssembly (committed 133-fn corpus: op-coverage, 57 execution-verified under wasmtime)
groups.axis_label: opcodes lowered out of the 1034 an external disassembler counts across the same 38 parseable modules, %

bars.label: op-coverage
bars.detail: 1034 of the 1034 opcodes across the 38 parseable corpus modules are lowered, where the 1034 is not disrobe's own count: wasm-tools 1.250.0 disassembled each committed .wat and its instruction inventory is pinned per fixture by BLAKE3 under crates/disrobe-pass-wasm-deob/tests/golden/external_wasm_op_inventory.json, so a decoder that stops seeing opcodes scores lower instead of shrinking its own denominator. That covers 133 of 133 functions across 38 parseable modules with every operator lowered and the emitted WAT re-assembling; the other 2 of the 40 corpus files are rejected by wasm-tools itself and are pinned with its error text, so this is 100% of the supported subset, NOT of all wasm. Lowering is not correctness: separately, 57 of 57 execution-eligible functions are EXECUTION-EQUIVALENT under wasmtime (original vs recovered: return values, trap parity, linear memory; 6 byte-identical), the remainder op-coverage-only
bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-wasm-deob/tests/external_op_denominator.rs divides 1034 lowered opcodes by the 1034 wasm-tools 1.250.0 counts over the same modules, and pins each fixture's hash so a changed corpus fails rather than re-scores; crates/disrobe-pass-wasm-deob/tests/semantic_recovery_corpus.rs measure() = 38 modules parsed / 2 skipped / 133 functions / fully_recovered==133, with the module count and function total pinned by equality and the recovered count floored at 133; tests/semantic_differential.rs = wasmtime execution differential, 57/57 execution-eligible equivalent (6 byte-identical), CI-runnable under --features sandbox; op-coverage is NOT execution-equivalence except for those 57

bars.label: execution-equivalence

verified_by.conditional: a module wasmtime declines to instantiate is skipped rather than failed, so eligibility is a filtered population narrower than the 133-function corpus. The eligible count is pinned by equality against this bar, so a run that reaches fewer functions fails instead of quietly shrinking what it is divided by

bars.detail: 57 of 57 execution-eligible functions in the same 38 parseable modules run equivalently under wasmtime: original against recovered on the same inputs, compared on return values, trap parity, and the first 4096 bytes of linear memory, 6 of them byte-identical. Eligibility is narrower than the op-coverage population because a function needs a callable signature and no host imports to be run at all
bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-wasm-deob/tests/semantic_differential.rs, CI-runnable under --features sandbox; this is the execution-equivalence leg and it is a different, smaller population than the 1034-opcode coverage bar beside it

groups.heading: JVM classfile (EdgeCases corpus, per-method real-javac recompile)
groups.axis_label: methods over the 131-method EdgeCases corpus, %; read each bar's own grading tier, because recompile-acceptance and execution-equivalence are different standards

bars.label: per-method
bars.detail: CI floor 131 of 131 (every top-level method recompiles error-free) measured under real javac attribution; the pickWord switch-expression lift (9afa2306) unmasked 25 latent defects previously hidden by javac parse-masking from the __unresolved__ token, all fixed by class: pattern-switch subject resolved to its source parameter (sealed-subtype exhaustiveness), sealed/permits emitted on inner type stubs, typed default initializers on final inner-stub fields, the Exceptions attribute threaded into a real throws clause, the loop-exhausted terminal emitted after a while loop whose exit is a shared pure-return tail, loop-captured locals hoisted to a fresh final declaration, and the shared return tail of an instanceof if-else-if chain duplicated under a Region-tree fall-through analysis
bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-jvm/tests/decompile_recompile_rate.rs (report_per_method_javac_recompile asserts ok >= PER_METHOD_JAVAC_OK_FLOOR 131 of PER_METHOD_JAVAC_TOTAL 131); CI runs it via the test job with actions/setup-java (JDK 25); floor measured 2026-06-22 after fixing the pickWord-unmasked defects

bars.label: per-method, execution-verified
bars.detail: 117 of the same 131 top-level methods are EXECUTION-equivalent, which is a strictly stronger standard than the recompile bar beside it: the original and the recovered source are each compiled by real javac, both are run under a real JVM, and every observable per-method result is compared. Read the residual 14 as the two separate populations it is, never as one: 8 methods are javac-clean and measurably DIVERGENT, and 6 are javac-clean but not executable in isolation (5 measure a nested-type stub, 1 is not self-reproducible), so those 6 are ungraded rather than passing. The distinction is not academic in this crate, which once emitted a method that compiled cleanly and incremented a counter twice on its exception path.
bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-jvm/tests/edgecases_execution_differential.rs (EXECUTION_EQUIVALENT_FLOOR 117 of PER_METHOD_TOTAL 131, with the equivalent set pinned as a membership list of method names rather than a count, so a method cannot leave it silently and the pinned-divergent lists only ever shrink); the reference is real javac plus a real JVM comparing observable behavior, never the decompiler's own output; the_execution_differential_reports_a_double_counted_exception_path injects a second counter increment on divSafe's recovered exception path and requires this differential to report divergence while javac still accepts the file; measured 117 equivalent, 8 divergent, 6 not driven on JDK 25

groups.heading: BEAM stripped Core Erlang (committed OTP 27.3.4 recompile-execution corpus)

bars.label: recompile-execution
bars.detail: Under OTP 27.3.4, 18 of the 19 explicitly named committed Erlang modules recover from BEAM with Dbgi and Docs stripped to Core Erlang source that recompiles, preserves the original export set, and returns the same observable result from the module's committed test/0 battery. This is a test/0 observation over each module, not a claim of equivalence for every possible input to every exported function.

groups.heading: Dalvik recovered bodies (committed dex corpus, real JVM verifier)
groups.axis_label: recovered classes that pass -Xverify:all, %

bars.label: verifier-clean (committed, CI)
bars.detail: 118 of 118 VERIFIER-PRESENTED classes in the committed EdgeCases/EdgeCasesKt/Hello dex pass the real JVM bytecode verifier (-Xverify:all) with 0 lifter verify failures, so the plotted figure is the verifier-presented ratio. State the other denominator too: the corpus holds 155 classes and 37 of them are link-skipped, never reaching the verifier because they reference supertypes the harness does not bundle, Kotlin's Function1 among them. That is a harness limit rather than a lifter defect, but it means 118 of 155 classes are verifier-attested and the remaining 37 are ungraded, not passing. A live-range-splitting pass recovers bodies with conflicting register types across joins, and 317 re-hosted method bodies verify clean with 0 failures, every non-stub recovered body re-hosted into an Object carrier and run through -Xverify:all. Floor 118 classes; the reference is the JVM rejecting malformed bytecode, not the lifter's own report.
bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-jvm/tests/dalvik_verifier_gate.rs (COMMITTED_VERIFY_CLEAN_CLASSES 118, COMMITTED_LIFTER_VERIFY_FAILURES 0, COMMITTED_CORPUS_CLASSES 155, COMMITTED_BODY_VERIFY_CLEAN 317, COMMITTED_BODY_VERIFY_FAILURES 0, every one an equality rather than a floor); reference = -Xverify:all over assemble_jar output, not the lifter self-report; measured 118 of 118 verifier-presented classes with 37 link-skipped and 317 re-hosted bodies clean on JDK 25, and because the corpus is committed and the translation deterministic, a figure that moves either way fails this gate until the documents state the new one

bars.label: body-lowering (real apks, local)

verified_by.conditional: the three apks are gitignored, so this gate re-measures only when DISROBE_RUN_REAL_APK_TESTS=1 and all three are present under corpus/mobile/apk/inbox; CI cannot re-derive either figure, and the numbers it pins are cross-checked against this file by dalvik_body_attest_bar_matches_the_pins_this_gate_enforces, which does run in CI

bars.detail: Two separate populations, stated separately. Self-reported body lowering: 82788 of 89516 defined methods across the three apks get a lowered body rather than a throw-stub, which is the lifter counting its own output (transmissionic 26192 of 27805 = 94.2, rustdesk 29376 of 32410 = 90.6, enrecipes 27220 of 29301 = 92.9). Verifier-attested: 2960 of 2994 recovered bodies presented to the real JVM pass -Xverify:all = 98.9 (transmissionic 980 of 993, rustdesk 1205 of 1216, enrecipes 775 of 785). The attested denominator is not the method count: 82756 non-stub candidate bodies, a deterministic 100-permille sample takes 8343, and 2994 of those can be re-hosted into an isolated Object carrier, so 5349 are excluded by harness limits and are ungraded rather than passing (1400 constructors, 1672 invokespecial receivers, 2128 unresolvable framework dependencies, 149 other). The apks are gitignored, so both figures are local; the committed-dex bar above is the CI-enforced attestation and its denominator is classes, not bodies.
bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-jvm/tests/dalvik_realworld_body_attest.rs (REAL_APK_METHOD_TOTAL 89516, SELF_REPORTED_BODIES 82788, CANDIDATE_BODIES 82756, SAMPLED_BODIES 8343, ATTESTED_PRESENTED 2994, ATTESTED_CLEAN 2960, ATTESTED_REJECTED 34, every one an equality rather than a floor, with the same counts pinned per apk in common::REAL_APKS and all 2994 verdicts pinned by name in tests/golden/dalvik_body_attest) and crates/disrobe-pass-jvm/tests/dex2jar_realworld_apks.rs (the same per-apk self-reported counts, also by equality); reference for the attested figure = java -Xverify:all rejecting malformed bytecode, not the lifter self-report

groups.heading: Detection and extraction breadth (counts, not percentages)
groups.axis_label: measured delivery / detected roster

bars.label: Containers
bars.detail: 100 formats detected, and each declares a payload extractor. 33 of them write member bytes from an input this repository commits, which is the measured leg. The other 67 have no committed input, so nothing here states whether their extractors work.
bars.source: ContainerKind enum crates/disrobe-binfmt/src/container.rs (ContainerKind::ALL is [Self; 100], 100 real variants excluding None), asserted in detected_count_is_one_hundred; every one of the 100 declares a payload extractor rather than a metadata summary or an external-tool hand-off, asserted in every_declared_format_carries_a_payload_extractor, which is a roster declaration and not a run. The delivered count is the measured leg: 33 of the 100 are driven to member bytes on disk by an input this repository commits, measured by crates/disrobe-cli/tests/container_breadth.rs over `git ls-files`, pinned in crates/disrobe-cli/tests/golden/container_breadth.txt and read back by published_container_counts_match_this_enum. The remaining 67 carry an extractor no committed input reaches, so they are unverified rather than shown to fail: absence of an input is not evidence of a broken extractor, and nothing here claims they work. The declared superset spans archives/installers (ZIP/tar/7z/RAR/cab/MSI/NSIS/deb/rpm/Docker/OCI/ISO), bare single-stream compression (gz/bz2/zst/lzma/lzip/lz4-frame/zlib/.Z), legacy archives (ar/arj/arc/lzh/lzop/uzip/xamarin-xalz/par2/ELF-overlay carve), embedded-linux filesystems (squashfs/cramfs/ext4/romfs/minixfs/jffs2/ubi-ubifs/yaffs/erofs/ntfs/android-sparse/btrfs-send), disk-image/partition containers (GPT/MBR/VHD/VHDX/WIM walked through FAT), and vendor firmware decryptors (D-Link AES/EnGenius XOR/Autel table/QNAP PC1 plus CRC-verified Netgear/Xiaomi/Tesla carves); a recursive carve-everything engine (multi-magic scan, chunk model, depth recursion, entropy gating) drives nested extraction. InnoSetup writes the decoded setup-data block stream (per-file split via the version-specific TSetupHeader parse is the documented limit) and InstallShield writes its stored and zlib members; the arj/arc/stuffit/partclone heavy codecs are carved verbatim with a documented note

bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-pyarmor/tests/static_unpack_corpus.rs named_v8_v9_default_trial_wrappers_decode_complete_root_code_objects binds the typed MANIFEST.toml roster to the discovered v8/v9 chunk-wrapper set, verifies each manifest-declared wrapper/runtime pair, checks the default-trial serial, statically decrypts every named wrapper, computes the header-declared marshal start, requires the public helper to agree, and requires disrobe-py-marshal to decode one complete root CodeObject. groups.heading: OLLVM control-flow-flattening dispatcher cover (committed two-function corpus)
groups.axis_label: dispatcher states the recovered program reaches / states the dispatcher can select

bars.label: OLLVM -fla dispatcher states
bars.denominator_label: states the two committed dispatchers can select
bars.detail: This is a cover, not an equivalence. The denominator is every state the dispatcher can select, read back out of each sample's own compare tree rather than typed into the gate, so a state the recovery never places stays in the denominator instead of shrinking it. classify_fla.bin declares 4 states and 4 are reached; sumto_fla.bin declares 5 and 5 are reached. The population is two functions built by ollvm-16 -fla and nothing else, so this states nothing about a flattened function this repository does not commit. Behavior is graded separately and more narrowly: a bounded stub_emu differential runs the flattened bytes and the re-emitted recovered bytes on 15 arguments per function, 60 executions in total, and compares the return value against corpus/native/ollvm/probe_src.c. That establishes agreement on those 15 arguments per function and on no other input.
bars.source: crates/disrobe-pass-native/tests/cff_dispatcher_cover.rs reads this file back and asserts both counts against what crates/disrobe-pass-native/src/deobf/cff.rs measures on the committed samples, so the binding runs from the crate to this data. dispatcher_cover_counts_every_state_the_flattened_dispatcher_can_select pins each sample's declared state count and requires every state to be covered, every transition to be resolved and the recovered edge set to pass its check. dropping_one_dispatcher_state_turns_the_cover_gate_red_and_names_it retargets one state store in classify_fla.bin, drops the cover to 3 of 4 and requires the gate to name the missing state, so the gate is not vacuous. a_bounded_differential_agrees_with_the_committed_source_on_every_input_it_runs executes both programs under stub_emu with a 200000-step and 16 KiB-stack budget, and a_seeded_wrong_edge_makes_the_bounded_differential_disagree retargets one recovered edge and requires disagreement on exactly the 6 arguments above ten. the_denominator_is_not_the_tree_walk_counting_itself recounts the same states a second way, by reading every equality compare against the state register out of a linear decode of the whole function, so a compare-tree walk that stopped early would shrink its own denominator and be caught here
